input.rationale: The fixed experiment 13bd8c6cd5cf4d318ed61aa3e6a05e6d-experiment has been executed and retained, so this update converts the malformed-proposal probe into an execution-grounded conclusion for question 13bd8c6cd5cf4d318ed61aa3e6a05e6d-question-0 and records the observed instance as durable knowledge: the undecodable conf-change payload aborted the leader both when stepped in directly and when relayed untouched by a follower, while the well-formed control of the same entry type was appended normally. The question is marked explained with the sourced behaviour entry as its premise, the relation to the earlier empty-payload read-index finding is stated as a shared family rather than merged, and the trusted-message-boundary question stays with human review.

knowledge.assertion: The proposal path decodes the conf-change payload and panics on a decode error, and the follower's forwarding hop neither decodes nor rejects it, which is what the execution observed on both probes.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (freshly elected three-voter clusters {1,2,3}, node 1 leader in term 1 with committed 1 and applied 1, fault-free in-process delivery), stepping a MsgProp carrying an EntryConfChangeV2 with the undecodable payload {0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff} directly into the leader panicked with the verbatim recovered value 'unexpected EOF' and left the last index unchanged at 1 (parsed index 1: leader_panicked true, last_index_before 1, last_index_after 1). Stepping the same proposal into follower 2 did not panic the follower, which forwarded exactly one MsgProp to node 1 (index 3: follower_panicked false, follower_messages 1, forwarded_to 1), and stepping that forwarded message into the leader panicked with the same recovered value 'unexpected EOF' while the last index stayed 1 (index 3: leader_panicked true). The control probe with a well-formed ConfChangeV2 of the same entry type was stepped into the leader without panicking and was appended (index 5: leader_panicked false, last_index_before 1, last_index_after 2).
knowledge.conditions: One executed in-process experiment with the fixed harness bytes of experiment 13bd8c6cd5cf4d318ed61aa3e6a05e6d-experiment (receipt 41c7e3db58b4436cb4f37208a4435f9c, exit 0, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors); the payloads were constructed by the harness, the proposals were stepped directly into the state machines, the relayed message was delivered by the harness, and no restart, snapshot, membership change or joint configuration was involved. interpretations.rationale: Receipt 41c7e3db58b4436cb4f37208a4435f9c is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, unchanged target files, no parsing errors, 6 parsed events). Comparison 0 declares that stepping a proposal with an undecodable conf-change payload directly into a leader does not abort the node; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 1, correlated to its own admission at index 0 (conf_proposal_setup for probe malformed/direct: data_len 4, leader 1, term 1, committed 1, applied 1, leader_state StateLeader). The measured operands are leader_panicked true with the verbatim recovered value 'unexpected EOF' and last_index_before 1 equal to last_index_after 1, so the abort happened while decoding the proposal and nothing reached the log. Comparison 1 declares that relaying the same malformed proposal through a follower does not let it abort the leader that decodes it; it is violated at index 3, correlated to its admission at index 2 (probe malformed/via-follower, via_follower true). That outcome event records follower_panicked false with follower_messages 1 and forwarded_to 1, together with leader_panicked true and recovered 'unexpected EOF', so the relay neither decoded the payload nor refused it and the abort simply moved one hop. Comparison 2 is the control of the same entry type and holds at index 5: the well-formed ConfChangeV2 was stepped into the leader with no panic and last_index moved from 1 to 2, which shows the path, the proposal shape and the harness are functional and that the abort is specific to the undecodable payload. The mechanism is the sourced one: stepLeader unmarshals the conf-change payload and panics on a decode error (raft.go:1305-1313), while stepFollower relays a proposal by rewriting m.To only (raft.go:1714-1724) with no term attached (raft.go:536-541), so no validation exists anywhere between the relaying member and the decode. Engineering significance: the violated predicate is that a proposal the node cannot decode must be rejected rather than converted into an abort, and the execution also establishes that the relay hop a normal follower performs for client proposals carries no protection; this is the same family as the earlier empty-Entries read-index abort but a different input path (proposal decoding versus an unchecked Entries[0] access) and a different reachability argument (a forwarded proposal is an ordinary path), so the two are recorded separately for review rather than merged.

knowledge.assertion: The decode panic is the only reaction on the proposal path (index 1: 'unexpected EOF', no log change) and the forwarding hop is transparent to it (index 3: follower panic false, one forwarded message, leader panic true).

counterevidence: The panic is deliberate in the captured source: the proposal path decodes a payload that the library's own conf-change producer marshals, so a decode failure can be read as an 'impossible unless the caller or peer is broken' state rather than an oversight.

The control probe (index 5) shows a well-formed conf change of the same entry type is appended normally, which isolates the abort to the payload rather than to the proposal path, the entry type or the harness.

The harness constructs the payload and steps messages directly; the transport and any application-level validation between peers are outside the captured snapshot, so end-to-end reachability through a real peer was not observed.
The legacy EntryConfChange entry type shares the unmarshal-and-panic shape in the same block but was not executed, so only the EntryConfChangeV2 variant is established by this execution.
The same family was already recorded for an empty-Entries MsgReadIndex; this execution adds a proposal-path instance and a relay-hop observation, and the two may be deduplicated by human review.
limitations: One executed instance per probe in one process with fault-free delivery; the payload is a harness-constructed undecodable byte sequence rather than a specific producer's output.
Only the direct and single-follower-relay paths were probed; the legacy entry type, multi-hop relaying and the transport layer were not exercised.
No state-machine or log effect is claimed, since the malformed payload never reaches the log.

interpretations.report_answer: 在快照代码上，把携带 EntryConfChangeV2、Data 为不可解码字节的 MsgProp 直接交给 leader，会在解码阶段 panic（recovered='unexpected EOF'），日志索引不变（last_index 1→1）；把同样的提案交给 follower 时不触发 panic，follower 原样转发 1 条 MsgProp 给 node 1，该转发消息送进 leader 后同样以 'unexpected EOF' panic。对照：同类型但格式正确的 conf change 被正常追加（last_index 1→2）。源码显示 stepLeader 对 conf-change 载荷做 Unmarshal 并在失败时 panic（raft.go:1305-1313），而 stepFollower 只改写 m.To 后转发、不解码载荷也不附加 term（raft.go:1714-1724、536-541），因此从转发者到解码者之间不存在校验。该现象与先前“空 Entries 的 MsgReadIndex 导致 panic”属于同一族的另一条输入路径（提案解码 vs 未检查的 Entries[0]），是否去重与是否构成缺陷由人工复核判定。

investigations.question: On a stable leader using ReadOnlySafe, can a ReadIndex request that carries an rctx equal to one that is still pending complete, or is that request silently discarded so that its requester receives no read index answer while the cluster keeps making progress?
investigations.hypothesis: The leader keys pending read requests by the rctx string only, so a second admission carrying an equal rctx is dropped without recording its own request message; when the single status completes, the answer is addressed to the first admission's requester and no answer is ever produced for the second requester, even though the leader stays leader and keeps satisfying quorum heartbeat acknowledgments.
investigations.discriminator: Drive two real voters to forward ReadIndex messages with equal rctx to the leader before any quorum acknowledgment, then deliver the quorum ack and eight further heartbeat rounds with acks from both followers; count read index answers per requester while confirming the leader stays in StateLeader. Controls: the identical shape with distinct rctxes (both requesters must be answered) and a single requester retrying its own rctx (that requester must be answered), which separate a duplicate-rctx admission loss from a broken harness or a generally stalled leader.

knowledge.assertion: The second admission with an equal rctx is discarded, so the leader keeps exactly one pending status and one stored request message for the two admissions.
Completion answers only the stored first request message, so a discarded equal-rctx admission produces neither a MsgReadIndexResp nor a ReadState.

counterevidence: node.go:218-229 states that callers must not reuse an rctx and that the reuse restriction is only lifted starting with release-3.7, so the silent drop may be the documented behaviour of this release-3.6 revision rather than an implementation error; this draft reports the mechanism and the observed starvation, and leaves that classification to human review.

The same-requester retry case is answered: when one requester retries its own rctx while the status is pending, the single response is addressed to that requester, so the observed starvation requires a requester whose equal-rctx message is discarded because another requester was admitted first.

Existing test coverage (raft_test.go:1192-1222) exercises one unique rctx and only checks that the queue and pending map drain; node_test.go:196-241 forwards two equal rctxes from different nodes but asserts only that the messages are forwarded and never checks for read index answers.
limitations: Only ReadOnlySafe is exercised; ReadOnlyLeaseBased and the pendingReadIndexMessages path (a leader that has not yet committed an entry in its term) are out of scope for this experiment.
The observation window is eight leader heartbeat rounds with quorum acknowledgments in one process; it establishes repeated nonprogress under normal opportunities rather than an unbounded guarantee.
The requester-side application contract (matching ReadStates by RequestCtx) is read from node.go / rawnode.go rather than executed.

investigations.question: Can a MsgReadIndex with an empty Entries slice reach the leader's read-index producer and panic the node, or is the message rejected, dropped or validated before the producer dereferences Entries[0]?
investigations.hypothesis: MsgReadIndex is sent and forwarded without a term (raft.go:536-541 keeps the local-message treatment for MsgProp/MsgReadIndex), a follower forwards it unchanged to its leader while a leader passes it straight to sendMsgReadIndexResponse (raft.go:1759-1765, 1346-1363), and that producer dereferences m.Entries[0] in readOnly.addRequest and responseToReadIndexReq without checking the slice length; only MsgReadIndexResp has an entry-count check (raft.go:1766-1772) and only MsgProp has an explicit empty-entry panic (raft.go:1286-1289). The apparent mismatch is therefore that the same message shape is validated for the response direction and for proposals but not for the request direction entering the leader's producer.
investigations.discriminator: Step a MsgReadIndex carrying no Entries into a follower (expected: forwarded to its leader, raft.go:1759-1765) and into a leader (expected by this hypothesis: an index-out-of-range panic inside the read-index producer), then step a well-formed one-entry MsgReadIndex into the same node as a positive control. Use a recovering wrapper that records the recovered value plus the leader's state, term and readOnly queue/pending sizes at the moment of the panic, and compare with the empty-MsgProp path that panics deliberately. If the empty-Entries message is instead dropped, converted to an error or silently ignored, the hypothesis is refuted and the observed disposition is the finding.

knowledge.assertion: readOnly.addRequest uses m.Entries[0].Data as the request key, which is the unchecked access that aborts on an empty payload.
responseToReadIndexReq answers the stored request through req.Entries[0].Data, so the same unchecked premise exists on the completion path.

limitations: A malformed or forged peer message may be considered outside the trusted transport contract, so a panic here would be an availability/robustness question rather than a divergence from consensus; the question is registered to establish the actual behaviour first.
The discriminator has not been executed yet; the hypothesis is provisional and rests only on the captured dispatch and producer code.
The node-to-transport boundary is not part of the captured package, so reachability through a real peer depends on what the embedding application forwards to Node.Step.

investigations.question: When a conf change proposal fails the leader's propose-time validation, the leader replaces the entry with an empty EntryNormal and appends it while returning no error: can the proposing caller distinguish a discarded configuration change from an accepted one through the proposal result, and what does the log carry instead?
investigations.hypothesis: The conversion at raft.go:1333 keeps the proposal accepted: appendEntry succeeds, the returned error stays nil, the proposed index receives a normal entry with no data, pendingConfIndex is deliberately left untouched so the failed change is not treated as pending, and the resulting ConfState never changes, so a caller that only inspects the proposal result (nil error, committed index) cannot tell that its membership change was dropped. The apparent mismatch is between the proposal API's success signal and the responsibility to establish that the requested configuration change was admitted.
investigations.discriminator: On a leader in a simple (non-joint) configuration, propose a ConfChangeV2 with no changes and record (i) the error returned by Step, (ii) the type and Data length of the entry appended at the proposed index, (iii) the ConfState before and after that entry is committed and applied, and (iv) whether a second conf change proposed while one is pending is converted in the same way. Run the same proposal with DisableConfChangeValidation enabled as the control that must bypass the conversion, and compare with a valid single-node conf change as the positive control that must reach the applied ConfState. If the proposal error or the applied entry type/ConfState turn out to carry the distinction, the hypothesis is refuted.
counterevidence: The conversion is deliberate in the captured source: it is guarded by !r.disableConfChangeValidation, preceded by an Infof line naming the failed check, and Config.DisableConfChangeValidation documents propose-time verification as a feature, so a reviewer may read the empty-normal-entry substitution as intended behaviour rather than a silent drop.

The applying application sees the entry type when it applies the log, so an embedding server can in principle detect that its conf change became a normal entry; the question is about the proposal result and about what the library, not the embedding, guarantees.
limitations: No execution has been run for this question yet; the hypothesis rests only on the captured producer and the configuration documentation.
The discriminator covers a simple configuration and the empty-change case; joint configurations, learner changes and removals are separate branches of the same validation block.
Client-visible membership semantics of an embedding application (for example etcd's conf-change waiters) are outside the captured package.

investigations.question: When a committed configuration change removes the current leader and Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false, does the cluster still reach a new leader, or does the ineligible leader keep the leadership role and its heartbeats reset every eligible voter so that no proposal can commit and no election can complete without external intervention?
investigations.hypothesis: switchToConfig keeps the leadership role for a node that is absent from the new configuration when step-down is not requested, stepLeader then drops every proposal because the leader has no progress entry, and tickHeartbeat keeps broadcasting heartbeats that reset every remaining voter's election timer, so the cluster can neither commit client writes nor elect a replacement; with StepDownOnRemoval=true the same applied change makes the node a follower and the remaining voters elect a new leader.
investigations.discriminator: Propose, replicate and apply a ConfChangeV2 that removes node 1 on a three-voter cluster, then tick every node for a fixed number of rounds with prompt message delivery and record node states, whether a new leader was elected, the last index and committed index, and the proposal errors on the leader and on a forwarding follower; repeat with StepDownOnRemoval=true as the control. Also probe the read path on the ineligible leader with one and then a quorum of acknowledgments from the current voters. If the ineligible leader is eventually replaced, or if the followers campaign despite the heartbeats, the hypothesis is refuted.
limitations: The harness drives timers by ticking each node once per round in a fixed order, which is a legitimate but synthetic schedule; a real deployment also has network and scheduling jitter.
The probe covers simple removal of the leader in a three-voter cluster; joint configurations, learner demotion and multi-node changes are not exercised.
Whether StepDownOnRemoval=false is the right default for an embedding service, and whether an operator is expected to intervene, is a contract question outside the captured package.

investigations.question: When a second ReadIndex request is admitted with an rctx equal to one that is still pending, does the answer produced for that admission carry a read index at least as new as the leader's commit index observed at the second admission, or does it carry the first admission's older index?
investigations.hypothesis: readOnly.addRequest stores the read index only for the first admission with a given rctx (read_only.go:56-63), so a second admission with the same rctx creates no status of its own and the single answer produced on acknowledgment uses the first admission's stored index (raft.go:1596-1606, 2068-2084). If the leader committed an entry between the two admissions, the answer delivered for the later admission is older than that admission's commit index.
investigations.discriminator: On a three-voter cluster, forward ReadIndex with rctx X from follower 2, hold the resulting heartbeats so the status stays pending, commit a write through the real replication path, then admit a second ReadIndex with the same rctx X and deliver the follower acknowledgments; record the commit index at each admission and the index carried by the answer for X. Repeat with distinct rctxes as the control, where the second admission must have its own status and its answer must carry the newer index. If the coalesced answer carries the later index, or if the control behaves the same way, the hypothesis is refuted.

knowledge.assertion: The second admission with an equal rctx keeps exactly one pending status and stores no request message of its own, so no per-admission index exists for it.

limitations: The harness plays the application duties (holding and later delivering messages, and driving the followers' Step calls); no real transport is involved.
Only one interleaving is probed: one write committed between the two admissions in a three-voter cluster with the default ReadOnlySafe.

Whether an embedding application is allowed to reuse an rctx for a distinct read request is a contract question; release-3.6 documentation forbids it while the same comment states the restriction is lifted from release-3.7, so the finding is about the producer's index association, not about an application contract.

investigations.question: Does a ReadIndex request that reaches a leader before it has committed an entry in its current term get delivered once that first commit happens, or can it remain queued while the leader keeps making progress?
investigations.hypothesis: A MsgReadIndex submitted before the leader's first commit in its term is appended to r.pendingReadIndexMessages with no heartbeat broadcast, and the queue is drained only in the MsgAppResp-driven commit path, which the leader's own first commit in the term triggers; the queued request is then served by the usual ReadOnlySafe path.
investigations.discriminator: Make a node win an election without any follower acknowledging its entry, submit a local ReadIndex while committedEntryInCurrentTerm is false, and record the queue size, the emitted heartbeats and the delivered read states; then deliver the replicated entry to the followers, step their acknowledgments back, and record whether the queued request is released and delivered with the new commit index. The same probe also submits a ReadIndex after that commit as the contrast path. If the queued request stays queued after the commit, or if it was answered before the commit, the hypothesis is refuted.

knowledge.assertion: The deferred path holds the request in pendingReadIndexMessages with no heartbeat and releases it through the MsgAppResp commit path, which is what the execution observed.

limitations: The probe submits the read request from the leader itself, so the delivered read state is the leader's own; a forwarded request from a follower would additionally exercise the MsgReadIndexResp path.

The leader is put into its pre-commit state by calling becomeCandidate/becomeLeader directly instead of waiting for an election round trip, because the intermediate state is otherwise not observable; the state itself is the library's normal post-election state.
Only the default ReadOnlySafe and a three-voter cluster are covered.

investigations.question: On a stable leader using ReadOnlySafe, can a ReadIndex request that carries an rctx equal to one that is still pending complete, or is that request silently discarded so that its requester receives no read index answer while the cluster keeps making progress?
investigations.hypothesis: The leader keys pending read requests by the rctx string only, so a second admission carrying an equal rctx is dropped without recording its own request message; when the single status completes, the answer is addressed to the first admission's requester and no answer is ever produced for the second requester, even though the leader stays leader and keeps satisfying quorum heartbeat acknowledgments.
investigations.discriminator: Drive two real voters to forward ReadIndex messages with equal rctx to the leader before any quorum acknowledgment, then deliver the quorum ack and eight further heartbeat rounds with acks from both followers; count read index answers per requester while confirming the leader stays in StateLeader. Controls: the identical shape with distinct rctxes (both requesters must be answered) and a single requester retrying its own rctx (that requester must be answered), which separate a duplicate-rctx admission loss from a broken harness or a generally stalled leader.

knowledge.assertion: The second admission with an equal rctx is discarded, so the leader keeps exactly one pending status and one stored request message for the two admissions.
Completion answers only the stored first request message, so a discarded equal-rctx admission produces neither a MsgReadIndexResp nor a ReadState.

counterevidence: node.go:218-229 states that callers must not reuse an rctx and that the reuse restriction is only lifted starting with release-3.7, so the silent drop may be the documented behaviour of this release-3.6 revision rather than an implementation error; this draft reports the mechanism and the observed starvation, and leaves that classification to human review.

The same-requester retry case is answered: when one requester retries its own rctx while the status is pending, the single response is addressed to that requester, so the observed starvation requires a requester whose equal-rctx message is discarded because another requester was admitted first.

Existing test coverage (raft_test.go:1192-1222) exercises one unique rctx and only checks that the queue and pending map drain; node_test.go:196-241 forwards two equal rctxes from different nodes but asserts only that the messages are forwarded and never checks for read index answers.
limitations: Only ReadOnlySafe is exercised; ReadOnlyLeaseBased and the pendingReadIndexMessages path (a leader that has not yet committed an entry in its term) are out of scope for this experiment.
The observation window is eight leader heartbeat rounds with quorum acknowledgments in one process; it establishes repeated nonprogress under normal opportunities rather than an unbounded guarantee.
The requester-side application contract (matching ReadStates by RequestCtx) is read from node.go / rawnode.go rather than executed.

investigations.question: When a conf change proposal fails the leader's propose-time validation, the leader replaces the entry with an empty EntryNormal and appends it while returning no error: can the proposing caller distinguish a discarded configuration change from an accepted one through the proposal result, and what does the log carry instead?

knowledge.statement: In StateLeader with the ReadOnlySafe option, when a MsgReadIndex arrives whose Entries[0].Data equals the rctx of a request that is already recorded in readOnly.pendingReadIndex, readOnly.addRequest returns early without storing the new request message, and sendMsgReadIndexResponse still attaches a heartbeat with that rctx (bcastHeartbeatWithCtx) and re-acknowledges the local node; the readIndexQueue and pendingReadIndex therefore keep exactly one status for the two admissions, and no second request message is retained.
knowledge.conditions: Node is in StateLeader, ReadOnlyOption is ReadOnlySafe (the default), the leader has committed an entry in its current term so stepLeader calls sendMsgReadIndexResponse directly, the earlier request with the equal rctx is still pending (not yet advanced), and no reset/become* has occurred between the two admissions.

knowledge.statement: On the acknowledging heartbeat, stepLeader asks readOnly.advance for the statuses up to the acknowledged ctx and then answers each returned status through responseToReadIndexReq(rs.req, rs.index): a status whose stored request came from a remote peer produces one MsgReadIndexResp addressed to that stored request's From, and a status whose stored request came from the leader itself appends one local ReadState. Only the request message of the first admission with a given rctx is stored, so admissions that were discarded by addRequest produce no read index answer of either kind.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe with a quorum of heartbeat acknowledgments carrying the ctx, leader state unchanged between admission and acknowledgment, and the discarded admission having used the same rctx bytes as the stored one.

knowledge.statement: In the retained execution of the fixed experiment (three-voter cluster {1,2,3} in one process, node 1 leader in term 1 with a committed entry in its term, ReadOnlySafe, fault-free ordered delivery), the ReadIndex request admitted first (parsed event 1, requester 2, rctx 'assurance-dup-rctx') received one MsgReadIndexResp and one ReadState, while the equal-rctx request admitted second (event 2, requester 3) received no MsgReadIndexResp and no ReadState (event 13: responded=false, responses=0, requester_read_states=0) over the following eight leader heartbeat rounds (events 4-11: leader_state=StateLeader, pending=0, undelivered=0, cumulative responses_to_3=0) whose acknowledgments were produced by the real follower state machines. With two different rctxes both requesters were answered (events 15-18), and with a single requester retrying its own rctx that requester was answered (events 20-21).

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 5827db69173840a595c972e79565bcde is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors, 22 parsed events). Comparison 0 asks whether every admitted ReadIndex request that carries an rctx equal to another requester's pending rctx receives a read index answer; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 13. Event 13 is the delivery observation for request_id 'duplicate/3' with responded=false, responses=0, requester_read_states=0 and rounds_waited=8, and the prerequisite correlation links it to its own admission at index 2 (read_index_request for requester 3, rctx 'assurance-dup-rctx'), whose measured operands are pending_after=1 and queue_after=1: the admission produced no new pending status compared with requester 2's admission at index 1. Index 12 is the matched positive counterpart for request_id 'duplicate/2' (responded=true, responses=1), so the two admissions differ only in requester identity. Index 3 records a third, identical retry from requester 3: it was stepped into the leader (two heartbeats emitted, leader_state=StateLeader) while queue_before=1 and queue_after=1, so the retry was processed and discarded in the same way and no error was returned on the caller path (rawnode.go:560-563 discards the Step error). Events 4-11 are the observation window: the leader stayed in StateLeader with pending=0, queue=0, undelivered=0 and cumulative responses_to_3=0 across eight rounds in which the heartbeat acknowledgments were produced by the real follower state machines, so repeated nonprogress is not attributable to a stalled leader, an unprocessed message queue or a lost quorum. The mechanism is the sourced one: readOnly.addRequest discards a second admission with an equal rctx without storing its request message (read_only.go:56-63), and completion answers only rs.req through responseToReadIndexReq (raft.go:1596-1606, 2068-2084), so the discarded admission can never receive either a local ReadState or a MsgReadIndexResp. The two controls exclude alternative explanations with the same sampling and the same delivery mechanics: comparison 1 (identical shape, distinct rctxes) holds at indices 17 and 18, and comparison 2 (a single requester retrying its own rctx) holds at index 21, so the read path itself, the harness and the leader's progress are functional. This is a bounded liveness result for the documented caller contract: node.go:218-229 tells callers that a lost ReadIndex request is theirs to retry and asserts that reusing an rctx is supported from release-3.7 on, while the observed behaviour silently discards such a retry instead of answering it.

knowledge.assertion: The equal-rctx admission is discarded at admission time (pending_after/queue_after unchanged at parsed indices 1 and 2).
Completion answers only the first admission's request message, which is why index 13 shows no response for requester 3 while index 12 shows the response for requester 2.

counterevidence: node.go:218-229 documents that callers must not reuse an rctx in release-3.6 and only states that the restriction is lifted starting with release-3.7, so the silent drop can be read as the documented restriction of this revision rather than an implementation error; the execution establishes the mechanism and the starvation, and the classification is left to human review.

The same-requester retry is answered (index 21), so the finding does not generalise to every retry: starvation was only observed when a different requester's equal-rctx admission was discarded because another requester had been admitted first.

The distinct-rctx control holds (indices 17 and 18), which shows the read path and the harness deliver answers when admissions are not coalesced; the violation therefore depends on rctx equality rather than on a generally broken experiment.
Only one execution in one process is cited; the eight-round window and the fault-free delivery assumption bound what the observation supports.
limitations: ReadOnlyLeaseBased, the pendingReadIndexMessages path for a leader without a committed entry in its term, membership change, snapshots, restarts and leadership change were not exercised.

The requester-side application contract (matching ReadStates by RequestCtx) is taken from node.go / rawnode.go rather than executed, so the observation is about the producer's answers, not about an application-level read result.
The retained execution establishes repeated nonprogress under normal quorum acknowledgments in one run; it is not an unbounded guarantee and does not exclude a future or external repair.
Whether a coalesced duplicate rctx can additionally mis-attribute a stale read index to a later distinct read request was not investigated.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 1e153b8ca3e64a7690ac91e69712c778 is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, changed_target_files [], no parsing errors, 20 parsed events). Comparison 0 declares that stepping a MsgReadIndex with no Entries into a leader must not panic the node; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 2, correlated to its own admission at index 1 (read_index_step for probe_id leader/empty-entries, role leader, entries 0, message MsgReadIndex, target node 1, term 1, log_committed 1). The outcome event records panicked=true with the verbatim recovered value 'runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0', messages_emitted=0, and state_after_step=StateLeader, term_after_step=1, pending_after_step=0, queue_after_step=0, committed_after_step=1, so the abort happens inside the read-index producer before any bookkeeping or message is produced. The harness is the only place that recovers the panic, which means the same value escapes (*raft).Step in production and aborts the caller's raft loop. Comparison 1 is the positive control on the same role with a one-entry payload and holds at index 6 (panicked=false, emitted_by_type {MsgHeartbeat:2}, pending_after_step=1, queue_after_step=1), so the probe method, the leader state and the producer itself work and the abort is specific to the empty payload. Comparison 2 covers the forwarding hop and holds at indices 14 and 18 (panicked=false, exactly one forwarded MsgReadIndex to node 1 in each case): a follower neither validates nor rejects the empty-payload read-index message, it relays it toward the leader, where the crossing into the leader's producer is what aborts. Comparison 3 is the guarded contrast in the same file and holds at index 10 (panicked=true, recovered '1 stepped empty MsgProp'), confirming that the package does abort deliberately on an empty payload elsewhere. The mechanical premise is sourced: readOnly.addRequest reads m.Entries[0].Data (read_only.go:56-63) and responseToReadIndexReq reads req.Entries[0].Data (raft.go:2071-2083); the only entry-count validation on the read-index path belongs to MsgReadIndexResp (raft.go:1766-1772); MsgReadIndex is dispatched without a term check and forwarded unchanged (raft.go:536-541, 1759-1765, 1346-1363); the library's own producer always attaches exactly one entry (rawnode.go:560-563). Predicate meaning is preserved: the violated predicate is 'a peer-delivered message shape does not abort the node', as evaluated on a leader of a healthy three-voter cluster with an otherwise idle log. Engineering significance is separate and deliberately left to review: the same package both validates a peer entry count on the response direction and aborts on an empty proposal payload, so this witness shows an unchecked payload assumption on the request direction rather than settling whether the abort is intended.

knowledge.assertion: The panic is the unchecked m.Entries[0].Data access of the read-index admission path.
The completion path reads req.Entries[0].Data, so the same payload assumption is shared by the answering side.

counterevidence: The captured package also aborts on an empty proposal payload: stepping MsgProp with no Entries into the leader panicked with the library's own message '1 stepped empty MsgProp' (parsed index 10), and proposals reach a leader through the same term-less forwarding path (raft.go:536-541 and stepFollower's MsgProp case). The empty-Entries MsgReadIndex abort can therefore be read as the library's intended stance on payload shapes its own producers never emit, not as an implementation error.

Counter-stance inside the same file: the read-index response path validates the entry count of a peer-delivered message and logs an error instead of aborting (raft.go:1766-1772), so the codebase also contains a remote-input validation stance for the same message family.

The captured package contains no producer of an empty-Entries MsgReadIndex (rawnode.go:560-563 always attaches one entry), so the probed shape has no legitimate in-package origin and its reachability depends on a caller or peer that crafts it.

The probe constructs the pb.Message directly and steps it; the transport, admission control and any application-level validation are outside the captured package, so end-to-end reachability was not observed.
limitations: The transport and application boundary are outside the captured snapshot, so this witness establishes the state machine's behaviour for the message shape, not that a real peer can deliver it.

Only a three-voter cluster with the default ReadOnlySafe was probed, and only leader and follower states: the pendingReadIndexMessages path (leader without a committed entry in its term), ReadOnlyLeaseBased, joint configurations and leader change were not exercised.
Each probe ran once on a freshly elected cluster in a single process; the process-level consequence of the unrecovered panic was not observed, only the recovered value escaping Step.

interpretations.report_title: 客户端可提议“移除最后一个 voter”并被提交，应用该条目时节点 panic（该变更事后才被拒绝）
interpretations.report_answer: 在快照代码上，单 voter 集群 {1} 中通过 MsgProp 提议移除 node 1：Step 返回 nil，条目写入索引 2 并提交（committed=true），随后按文档应用该已提交条目时 panic，recovered 文本为 'removed all voters'，配置保持 [1] 未变；对照的加节点变更为同样形状（提议成功、提交、应用无 panic，voters 变为 [1,2]）。源码显示拒绝发生在 changer 计算最终配置时（confchange/confchange.go:170-172，且该错误在 confchange/testdata/simple_safety.txt 中被当作预期行为），提议阶段的校验不计算最终 voter 集合（raft.go:1318-1335），而 applyConfChange 把任何 changer 错误直接 panic（raft.go:1961-1964，附 TODO 要求改为返回错误）。因此“拒绝”发生在提交与写入日志之后，进程级与重启后的后果未在本实验中观测，是否构成缺陷需人工结合调用方契约复核。

interpretations.rationale: Receipt d5f37430774c4bbd9d64967e3f82290d is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, unchanged target files, no parsing errors, 4 parsed events). Comparison 0 declares that after the node applied its own removal a proposal through the Node API is reported as not admissible instead of blocking until the caller's deadline; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 3, correlated to its own admission at index 2 (self_removal_applied for probe_id 'removed': node3_in_config false, voters [1,2], node3_lead 1, node3_state StateFollower, committed 3). The measured operands at index 3 are error_text 'context deadline exceeded', elapsed_ms 201 with timeout_ms 200, blocked_until_deadline true and node3_in_config false, so the call consumed the entire caller timeout and returned only the caller's own context error, carrying no statement that the node is no longer a member. Comparison 1 is the control with identical sampling and holds at index 1, correlated to its admission at index 0 (node_setup for probe_id 'member': leader 1, term 1, committed 1, node3_in_config true, caller timeout 200 ms): the same call returned no error in 0 ms while the node was a member, which shows the call, the timeout, the Node loop and the transport in the harness are functional and that the blocking behaviour depends on the applied removal. The mechanism is the sourced one: node.run disables the proposal channel when the node applies a configuration that no longer contains it (node.go:405-433, with the comment that this 'isn't very sound and likely has bugs' about re-enabling it on leadership change), and Node.Propose's wait path selects only on that channel, ctx.Done or n.done (node.go:513-537), so the library's own statement about admissibility on the proposal path (raft.go:1290-1295, the drop it returns when the removed node is the leader) is never produced here. Engineering significance: the predicate is about the signal a caller receives, and the observed value is that the only signal is the caller's own deadline, which a service using a non-expiring context would never receive, in which case the call would block for the lifetime of the node; that stronger case is recorded as unmeasured rather than observed.

knowledge.assertion: The disabled proposal channel is the reason the call can only complete on the caller's context, which is seen as elapsed 201 ms with the context error at index 3.

counterevidence: The block is deliberate in the captured source: node.run states that it blocks incoming proposals when the node was removed, so a reviewer may read the blocking behaviour as the intended mechanism rather than an implementation error.

The caller can bound the call: Node.Propose takes a context, and with a deadline it returns that deadline error, which is what the witness shows; only a caller that passes a non-expiring context would block indefinitely, and that case was not measured.

The raft layer does produce a drop statement on the proposal path when the removed node is the leader (raft.go:1290-1295), so the finding is about the Node layer's silence rather than about the library never signalling drops.
The control at index 1 shows the same call on the same node works normally while it is a member, which excludes a harness or transport failure as the cause.
Only the subject node applied the removal in this execution; the other voters were driven as bare raft instances, and the removal was applied through the Node API rather than by a full server loop.
limitations: One executed instance with a 200 ms caller context in one process and fault-free delivery; the observation is bounded to those conditions.
The behaviour with a non-expiring context, with a context cancelled by a server shutdown, and with the node stopped mid-call was not measured.

Only removal of a follower was exercised; removal of the leader takes a different branch (already covered by the earlier removed-leader finding), and joint configurations and learner demotion were not probed.

The embedding service's own proposal timeouts, retries and membership tracking are outside the captured package, so whether this behaviour is a practical hazard there and how it should be classified are left to human review.
interpretations.report_title: 节点被移除后 Node.Propose 只以调用方超时结束：没有“不可受理”的信号
interpretations.report_answer: 在快照代码上，三 voter 集群中把 node 3 交给 Node API 驱动：作为成员时同一 Node.Propose 调用 0ms 返回且 error 为 nil（对照）；在 leader 提议移除 node 3 并由其应用该已提交条目后（voters 变为 [1,2]，node3_in_config=false），同样的调用阻塞整段调用方超时（200ms，实测 201ms），最终只返回 'context deadline exceeded'，没有任何“该提案不可受理”的信息。源码显示 node.run 在节点应用了移除自身的配置后把提案通道置为 nil（node.go:405-433，且注释自称这种处理“isn't very sound and likely has bugs”），而 Node.Propose 的等待路径只能在该通道、调用方 context 或节点停止三者之一完成（node.go:513-537），因此 raft 层在同类情形下会给出的 drop 信号（raft.go:1290-1295，针对被移除的 leader）在这条路径上不会出现。若调用方使用不会到期的 context，调用将一直阻塞而没有任何信号——该更强情形未在本实验中测量；是否构成缺陷需人工结合调用方契约复核。

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 41c7e3db58b4436cb4f37208a4435f9c is a completed execution of this investigation's own experiment (status completed, exit 0, outcome tests_passed, unchanged target files, no parsing errors, 6 parsed events). Comparison 0 declares that stepping a proposal with an undecodable conf-change payload directly into a leader does not abort the node; it is violated with a complete valid witness at parsed index 1, correlated to its own admission at index 0 (conf_proposal_setup for probe malformed/direct: data_len 4, leader 1, term 1, committed 1, applied 1, leader_state StateLeader). The measured operands are leader_panicked true with the verbatim recovered value 'unexpected EOF' and last_index_before 1 equal to last_index_after 1, so the abort happened while decoding the proposal and nothing reached the log. Comparison 1 declares that relaying the same malformed proposal through a follower does not let it abort the leader that decodes it; it is violated at index 3, correlated to its admission at index 2 (probe malformed/via-follower, via_follower true). That outcome event records follower_panicked false with follower_messages 1 and forwarded_to 1, together with leader_panicked true and recovered 'unexpected EOF', so the relay neither decoded the payload nor refused it and the abort simply moved one hop. Comparison 2 is the control of the same entry type and holds at index 5: the well-formed ConfChangeV2 was stepped into the leader with no panic and last_index moved from 1 to 2, which shows the path, the proposal shape and the harness are functional and that the abort is specific to the undecodable payload. Engineering significance: the violated predicate is that a proposal the node cannot decode must be rejected rather than converted into an abort, and the execution also establishes that the relay hop a normal follower performs for client proposals carries no protection; this is the same family as the earlier empty-Entries read-index abort but a different input path (proposal decoding versus an unchecked Entries[0] access) and a different reachability argument (a forwarded proposal is an ordinary path), so the two are recorded separately for review rather than merged.

knowledge.assertion: The decode panic is the only reaction on the proposal path (index 1: 'unexpected EOF', no log change) and the forwarding hop is transparent to it (index 3: follower panic false, one forwarded message, leader panic true).

counterevidence: The panic is deliberate in the captured source: the proposal path decodes a payload that the library's own conf-change producer marshals, so a decode failure can be read as an 'impossible unless the caller or peer is broken' state rather than an oversight.

The control probe (index 5) shows a well-formed conf change of the same entry type is appended normally, which isolates the abort to the payload rather than to the proposal path, the entry type or the harness.

The harness constructs the payload and steps messages directly; the transport and any application-level validation between peers are outside the captured snapshot, so end-to-end reachability through a real peer was not observed.
The legacy EntryConfChange entry type shares the unmarshal-and-panic shape in the same block but was not executed, so only the EntryConfChangeV2 variant is established by this execution.
The same family was already recorded for an empty-Entries MsgReadIndex; this execution adds a proposal-path instance and a relay-hop observation, and the two may be deduplicated by human review.
limitations: One executed instance per probe in one process with fault-free delivery; the payload is a harness-constructed undecodable byte sequence rather than a specific producer's output.
Only the direct and single-follower-relay paths were probed; the legacy entry type, multi-hop relaying and the transport layer were not exercised.
No state-machine or log effect is claimed, since the malformed payload never reaches the log.

Whether a peer-produced proposal of this shape is within the trusted message contract is a question for human review, and so is the severity classification; no claim is made that a real deployment can deliver such a payload.
The relation to the earlier empty-Entries read-index abort is a shared mechanism family; this interpretation does not revise or close that finding.
